mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation surprises are strongly positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the following 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during NBER-defined recessions.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails when wage growth is accelerating.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and depresses earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong commodity price declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above 2.5% for two consecutive months signals a stagflation risk, which increases uncertainty and discount rates, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2.5% AND CPIAUCSL > 2.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails when oil prices fall sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A strong, sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals a recovery in residential investment, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of rising mortgage rates.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) over one month indicates a mixed labor market where job creation is insufficient to absorb new entrants, resulting in flat or negative earnings momentum and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE also increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails when wage growth accelerates.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings, which reduces consumer spending and corporate revenue expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of aggressive fiscal stimulus.
